claims.text: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing: EV-GPS-00111 records a trace of 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%. Both gates are crossed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms - and the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record is expressly not the field the threshold test runs on.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump between consecutive fixes. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and the rider is not put to proving it through any independent source.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00111, agree on the 07:47:40 pickup event, and the excess crosses the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has accordingly shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the PIE was bad that morning does not discharge it.

The rider's own record does not trigger the POL-RD-08 additional-corroboration rule: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. That factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven, and under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile bears on this test at all.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse any part of this detour. The chat log contains only the driver's own notification - 'i come off at bukit panjang ok', sent at 07:54:20, after he had already left the optimal corridor - and the rider's 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. Neither message is a rider instruction to take a particular road, both waypoint_hint fields are null, and the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 therefore cannot be run at all. Acquiescence in a decision the driver had already taken is not a rider-requested detour.

The driver's closure defence exonerates only if every limb of POL-RD-03 is made out, and the third limb is not established on this record: the actual route must leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment AND rejoin it after. The record places the rejoin on the AYE, while the trip_record describes the optimal route as the BKE southbound then the PIE westbound; no artifact puts the vehicle back on that corridor after the closure. The driver carries the burden under POL-RD-08, and on the face of the artifacts he has not shown the rejoin the clause requires, so the excess is not exonerated and falls to be refunded.

If the exoneration is not made out, the money is arithmetic and not discretionary. Against the booked optimal route, recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP and zero fixed surcharges = 31.00; charged_total was 37.74, so the refund is 6.74, payable rounded up to SGD 6.75. That is 17.9% of the amount charged, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider's entitlement on these figures is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The disputed charge is live and not already settled: the fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so anything short of a refund, or of an escalation that holds the sum, leaves the rider carrying the disputed SGD 8.00. A NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute is party-relative and is not a neutral outcome for this rider.

claims.text: The threshold showing is made out on this trip and nowhere else. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00111 and agree on the pickup/start at 2026-08-03T07:47:40+08:00, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the trace figure that governs under POL-RD-01 (trace_distance_km 29.98, not the rounded actual_distance_km 30.0) the excess over the booked optimal of 24.0 km is 5.98 km and 24.92% — past both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates. The burden therefore shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08, and the driver discharges it the way that clause requires: by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The excess is exonerated outright under POL-RD-03. The artefact is EV-ADVIS-00111-01, an LTA DataMall CLOSURE on the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit' — a segment the booked optimal route uses (the trip record's optimal_route_source is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'), so limb (a) is met. Its validity window is 07:10–09:30, bracketing the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip by far more than the 15-minute buffer limb (b) allows, with 41.5 minutes of overlap and overlaps_trip_window true. The 10-second, 100%-coverage trace on EV-GPS-00111 shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining it on the AYE, which is limb (c). All three conditions are satisfied.

The exoneration is not merely partial — it covers the whole measured excess. The POL-RD-03 cap is 1.30 x the ADDITIONAL distance of the shortest lawful alternative over the booked optimal, plus 1.0 km of tolerance: 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess is 5.98 km, which is less than 7.76 km, so justified_excess_km is the measured figure itself and there is no unexonerated residue left for POL-RD-02 to operate on.

The routing is the authority's own diversion, not a discretionary shortcut: the advisory text on EV-ADVIS-00111-01 reads 'Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd', which is exactly the road the rider's own claim text describes the driver using ('came off at Bukit Panjang and went down Upper Bukit Timah and around by the AYE'). The driver took the published way round a HIGH-severity closure of the corridor the optimal route uses.

Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal that POL-RD-03 requires — 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration scaled from the booked 30.0 min to 37.5 min — and the money simply is not there: recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against a charged_total of 37.74. The difference is SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so under POL-RD-02 read with POL-RD-03 the outcome is NO_ACTION and the charged fare of SGD 37.74 stands as recorded on EV-FARE-00111 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

There is no pass-through correction to add on top. EV-FARE-00111 records tolls_erp 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the trace crosses no gantry, so the standalone off-route ERP refund that POL-RD-09 gives even an exonerated closure has nothing to operate on and the SGD 12.00 cap on that head is not reached. The distance and time charges stand because POL-RD-03 places the closure beyond the driver's control, and the rider's own claim that he 'did not see any closure' does not put a gantry on the trace.

The chat log confirms the driver told the rider before he diverted — MSG-00111-001, sent 07:54:20, 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — and the rider read it and answered at 07:54:55, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', without objecting to the route. I do not put this forward as a rider-instructed detour and do not rely on POL-RD-04, because the rider requested no waypoint and waypoint_hint is null; it is offered as contemporaneous notice that corroborates the driver's account of why he left the corridor and rebuts any suggestion the diversion was concealed or self-serving.

No repeat-deviation scrutiny is engaged. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation — excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km absolute, on the excess REMAINING after adjustment — and after the POL-RD-03 cap is applied there is no remaining excess at all, while the raw figures (24.92%, 5.98 km) sit below both materiality thresholds. Were the profile consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, which establishes no pattern on the test POL-RD-06 actually states.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver: the trip's own telemetry shows the route really was longer than booked. EV-GPS-00111 records 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 5.98 km, 24.9%, past both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20%). I use the trace figure, which governs, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on EV-TRIP-00111. The threshold is therefore made out and the burden shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08. The driver is nonetheless excused under POL-RD-03. EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is an LTA DataMall closure of the PIE towards Tuas after Clementi Rd — a segment the booked optimal route uses (BKE southbound then PIE westbound); it ran 07:10–09:30, bracketing the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip; and the trace leaves that corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed stretch and rejoins it on the AYE afterwards. LTA's own diversion published with the advisory is 'via Upper Bukit Timah Rd' — the road the driver took. I do not accept the rider's argument that the rejoin on the AYE defeats limb (c): one-north is not on the PIE, the optimal route must leave the PIE to reach it, and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor before the closed segment and coming back onto the corridor after it — which is precisely the pattern limb (c) describes. The excuse is capped at the lesser of the measured excess and 1.30 × (29.2 − 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km, so the whole 5.98 km is justified and the closure-adjusted optimal is 29.98 km / 37.5 min. On that adjusted route, POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 × 29.98 + 0.28 × 37.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against charged_total 37.74 on EV-FARE-00111. The refund is 0.155, below the 0.50 de minimis, so no refund issues and the 37.74 charge stands. The rider's alternative figure of 6.74 (6.75 rounded up) is correct arithmetic against the booked route, but the booked route is not the baseline once POL-RD-03 excuses the excess. No pass-through correction is due: tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (229 fixes at 10 s, no gaps), so it decides the deviation on its own and needs no independent corroboration. No repeat-deviation pattern is engaged, so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises, and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The rider's 'I did not see any closure' is an assertion with no artifact behind it and does not outweigh the LTA advisory; the driver announced the diversion in the chat at 07:54:20 and the rider answered at 07:54:55 without objecting. On this rider-filed dispute, NO_ACTION leaves the charge as it stands: the SGD 37.74 fare is not refunded, and the SGD 8.00 in dispute is neither returned nor written off.

Rider and driver: this decides DSP-00111 on trip TRP-00111 (Woodlands to one-north, 3 Aug 2026; SGD 37.74 charged). The outcome is NO_ACTION — the fare stands and no money moves.

THE DEVIATION IS MEASURED, AND THE RIDER'S FIGURES ARE RIGHT. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace figure (29.98 km on EV-GPS-00111), not the rounded 30.0 km on the trip record, the governing measurement. Against the booked optimal of 24.0 km that is an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.92% — past both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates — so a deviation is established, and the burden shifted to the driver under POL-RD-08. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and no jumps, so the deviation stands on the trace alone.

THAT DEVIATION IS FULLY EXONERATED UNDER POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00111-01) closes the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — the expressway segment the booked route uses — from 07:10 to 09:30, bracketing the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip well inside the 15-minute buffer. The trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoining it after. The cap on that exoneration is 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km, and the measured excess of 5.98 km sits under it, so the whole excess is justified and no residue is left for a POL-RD-02 refund to operate on. Run the arithmetic against the closure-adjusted optimal (24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration scaled to 37.5 minutes): recomputed fare is SGD 37.585 (3.80 base + 22.485 distance + 10.50 time + 0.80 platform fee, no ERP), against the 37.74 charged. The 0.155 difference is below the 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is NO_ACTION.

ON THE RIDER'S OBJECTION that the route rejoins on the AYE and not on the PIE: we do not accept it. Both routes finish at one-north, which is served by the AYE, so the AYE carries the route to its destination and the rejoin there is a rejoin of the route the optimal follows after the closed segment; POL-RD-03(c) requires the vehicle to leave before the closed segment and rejoin after, which is what the trace shows. That reading is confirmed by the driver taking the authority's own posted diversion — 'Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd' — and by his 29.98 km being essentially the advisory's shortest lawful alternative of 29.2 km. The rider's alternative arithmetic (recomputed fare 31.00, refund 6.74 rounded to 6.75) would be the figure if the exoneration failed, but it does not fail, so that figure does not operate here.

POL-RD-04 IS NOT IN PLAY. The rider gave no instruction to take any particular road, both waypoint_hint fields are null, and 'as long as I reach by 8.30' identifies no place; the driver did not rely on a rider-requested detour and the excess is not excluded on that footing. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00111) is used only as contemporaneous notice that the driver told the rider of the closure before completing the diversion, and the driver's account is consistent with the advisory.

NO PASS-THROUGH CORRECTION ARISES. The fare breakdown records 0.00 of ERP and an empty gantry list, and the trace crosses no gantry, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to refund and its 12.00 cap is not reached. No repeat-deviation pattern is engaged under POL-RD-06 (0 flags in 90 days over 588 completed trips), so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows. No profile field below weight or outside POL-GEN-01's citable list was used. Every artifact here carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so no discount applies and the confidence floor is not breached. Because payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, the rider continues to pay the 37.74 — NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge as it stands; it does not re-create it. No clause in this case produces a referral, and no amount is held.

To the rider and the driver: the deviation is established, but it is fully exonerated, so the fare that was charged stands and no refund issues.

Rider — you are right that the trip ran longer than booked. EV-GPS-00111 records 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km: an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.9%, which crosses both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and the trip record, trace and fare breakdown all carry TRP-00111 with the same 07:47:40 start. But the driver was not taking a shortcut of his own choosing. EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is a live LTA DataMall closure — a lorry fire, all lanes closed on the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — on the very corridor the booked optimal route uses, with a 07:10–09:30 window that brackets the whole 07:47–08:25 trip. The trace shows the vehicle leaving that corridor before the closed stretch (off the BKE at Bukit Panjang) and rejoining the route after it (on the AYE), which is the POL-RD-03(c) pattern, and the driver took the authority's own published diversion ('Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd'). Your point that the rejoin was on the AYE rather than the PIE carriageway does not defeat the clause: the stretch being avoided was closed, so the rejoin can only be downstream.

The exoneration is capped at 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess of 5.98 km is inside that cap, so the whole excess is justified, and POL-RD-03 sets the closure-adjusted optimal at 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, 37.5 min. Running POL-RD-02 on that adjusted route: recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against a charged total of 37.74. The difference is SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no refund issues and the recorded charge stands (payment status CHARGED, refund issued 0.00). The alternative arithmetic you offer (recomputed 31.00, difference 6.74) runs against the booked optimal, and POL-RD-03 directs POL-RD-02 to run against the closure-adjusted one instead.

Driver — nothing further is owed to you either. No ERP or toll was charged (tolls_erp 0.00, no gantries on either route), so POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle, and there is no unbilled-distance shortfall, so POL-RD-04 compensation does not arise. The deviation is not MATERIAL (24.9% and 5.98 km are below the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds) and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 588 completed trips, so no POL-RD-06 driver-conduct referral arises either.

On the remaining points: POL-RD-04 does not run — the chat log holds only the driver's 07:54:20 notice, which the rider read and answered, with no waypoint requested — and both sides agree it cannot excuse anything. The rider's additional-corroboration rule is not engaged (deviation_claims_60d is 1, below 4). Every artifact in this pool carries weight 1.0, so no finding is discounted. The rider is correct that NO_ACTION leaves the charge in place; that is the outcome because, once the closure is allowed for, the fare charged matches the fare the trip should have cost.

To both of you, on TRP-00111 (Woodlands to one-north, 3 Aug 2026):

The deviation is real. On the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record — the drive was 29.98 km (EV-GPS-00111) against a booked optimal of 24.0 km (EV-TRIP-00111): an excess of 5.98 km and 24.92%. Both gates are crossed (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so a route deviation is established and the burden shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so the rider is not put to proving the deviation through any independent source, and no escalation arises under POL-RD-10(3).

The driver has discharged the shifted burden, and the closure exonerates the excess in full. EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is a genuine LTA DataMall CLOSURE (lorry fire, HIGH severity) on the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit — the corridor the booked optimal route uses, with intersects_route true — and its window 07:10–09:30 brackets the whole trip (07:47:40–08:25:40) with 41.5 minutes of overlap. The unimpaired trace shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining it on the AYE afterwards, which is the advisory's own published diversion ('Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd') and matches the route the rider describes in the complaint. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met. The rider's argument that the rejoin had to fall on the literal roads named in the routing summary does not succeed: the summary in optimal_route_source is a description, not a road-by-road definition of the corridor, the trace is complete and shows the rejoin, and the driver's route is within 0.78 km of the shortest lawful alternative (29.98 vs 29.2 km). All three limbs of the driver's closure defence are therefore accepted; the rider's limb (c) objection is rejected for those reasons.

The cap does not bite. POL-RD-03 caps exoneration at 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km, and the measured excess is 5.98 km, so justified_excess_km is the whole of it and no residue is left for POL-RD-02 to work on.

The money then falls out. Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal the clause requires — 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration scaled 30.0 x 29.98/24.0 = 37.5 min — and the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x the 1.0 surge on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus 0.00 ERP = 37.585. Charged_total was 37.74 (EV-FARE-00111), so the residual refund is 0.155 — below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, which makes the outcome NO_ACTION. The charged fare of 37.74 stands and refund_issued_sgd stays at 0.00. That is not a finding against you, rider: the deviation was established, but the closure left nothing payable above five cents. The rider's alternative computation against the booked optimal (recomputed 31.00, refund 6.74, payable 6.75) is rejected because it is the figure that applies only if the exoneration fails, and it does not.

There is nothing to correct on the pass-through lines. tolls_erp is 0.00, erp_gantries is empty and the trace crosses no gantry, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle and no billing-integrity referral issues. No rider-requested detour engages POL-RD-04 (waypoint_hint is null and the chat log contains only the driver's own notice and the rider's 'as long as i reach by 8.30', which is notice, not an instruction — so no driver compensation is due either). No repeat-deviation review is engaged under POL-RD-06: after the adjustment no excess remains, the raw figures (24.92%, 5.98 km) sit below both materiality thresholds, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established and no conduct referral issues. The rider profile decides nothing: deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4 that POL-RD-08 requires before extra corroboration is needed.

Every artifact relied on carries weight_multiplier 1.0 and none is impaired, so nothing is discounted under POL-GEN-02 and the confidence cap is 1.0. Confidence 0.9.

ledger.claim: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing: EV-GPS-00111 records a trace of 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%. Both gates are crossed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms - and the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record is expressly not the field the threshold test runs on.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump between consecutive fixes. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and the rider is not put to proving it through any independent source.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00111, agree on the 07:47:40 pickup event, and the excess crosses the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has accordingly shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the PIE was bad that morning does not discharge it.

The rider's own record does not trigger the POL-RD-08 additional-corroboration rule: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. That factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven, and under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile bears on this test at all.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse any part of this detour. The chat log contains only the driver's own notification - 'i come off at bukit panjang ok', sent at 07:54:20, after he had already left the optimal corridor - and the rider's 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. Neither message is a rider instruction to take a particular road, both waypoint_hint fields are null, and the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 therefore cannot be run at all. Acquiescence in a decision the driver had already taken is not a rider-requested detour.

The driver's closure defence exonerates only if every limb of POL-RD-03 is made out, and the third limb is not established on this record: the actual route must leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment AND rejoin it after. The record places the rejoin on the AYE, while the trip_record describes the optimal route as the BKE southbound then the PIE westbound; no artifact puts the vehicle back on that corridor after the closure. The driver carries the burden under POL-RD-08, and on the face of the artifacts he has not shown the rejoin the clause requires, so the excess is not exonerated and falls to be refunded.

If the exoneration is not made out, the money is arithmetic and not discretionary. Against the booked optimal route, recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP and zero fixed surcharges = 31.00; charged_total was 37.74, so the refund is 6.74, payable rounded up to SGD 6.75. That is 17.9% of the amount charged, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider's entitlement on these figures is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The disputed charge is live and not already settled: the fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so anything short of a refund, or of an escalation that holds the sum, leaves the rider carrying the disputed SGD 8.00. A NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute is party-relative and is not a neutral outcome for this rider.

The threshold showing is made out on this trip and nowhere else. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00111 and agree on the pickup/start at 2026-08-03T07:47:40+08:00, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the trace figure that governs under POL-RD-01 (trace_distance_km 29.98, not the rounded actual_distance_km 30.0) the excess over the booked optimal of 24.0 km is 5.98 km and 24.92% — past both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates. The burden therefore shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08, and the driver discharges it the way that clause requires: by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The excess is exonerated outright under POL-RD-03. The artefact is EV-ADVIS-00111-01, an LTA DataMall CLOSURE on the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit' — a segment the booked optimal route uses (the trip record's optimal_route_source is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'), so limb (a) is met. Its validity window is 07:10–09:30, bracketing the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip by far more than the 15-minute buffer limb (b) allows, with 41.5 minutes of overlap and overlaps_trip_window true. The 10-second, 100%-coverage trace on EV-GPS-00111 shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining it on the AYE, which is limb (c). All three conditions are satisfied.

The exoneration is not merely partial — it covers the whole measured excess. The POL-RD-03 cap is 1.30 x the ADDITIONAL distance of the shortest lawful alternative over the booked optimal, plus 1.0 km of tolerance: 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess is 5.98 km, which is less than 7.76 km, so justified_excess_km is the measured figure itself and there is no unexonerated residue left for POL-RD-02 to operate on.

The routing is the authority's own diversion, not a discretionary shortcut: the advisory text on EV-ADVIS-00111-01 reads 'Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd', which is exactly the road the rider's own claim text describes the driver using ('came off at Bukit Panjang and went down Upper Bukit Timah and around by the AYE'). The driver took the published way round a HIGH-severity closure of the corridor the optimal route uses.

Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal that POL-RD-03 requires — 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration scaled from the booked 30.0 min to 37.5 min — and the money simply is not there: recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against a charged_total of 37.74. The difference is SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so under POL-RD-02 read with POL-RD-03 the outcome is NO_ACTION and the charged fare of SGD 37.74 stands as recorded on EV-FARE-00111 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

There is no pass-through correction to add on top. EV-FARE-00111 records tolls_erp 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the trace crosses no gantry, so the standalone off-route ERP refund that POL-RD-09 gives even an exonerated closure has nothing to operate on and the SGD 12.00 cap on that head is not reached. The distance and time charges stand because POL-RD-03 places the closure beyond the driver's control, and the rider's own claim that he 'did not see any closure' does not put a gantry on the trace.

The chat log confirms the driver told the rider before he diverted — MSG-00111-001, sent 07:54:20, 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — and the rider read it and answered at 07:54:55, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', without objecting to the route. I do not put this forward as a rider-instructed detour and do not rely on POL-RD-04, because the rider requested no waypoint and waypoint_hint is null; it is offered as contemporaneous notice that corroborates the driver's account of why he left the corridor and rebuts any suggestion the diversion was concealed or self-serving.

No repeat-deviation scrutiny is engaged. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation — excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km absolute, on the excess REMAINING after adjustment — and after the POL-RD-03 cap is applied there is no remaining excess at all, while the raw figures (24.92%, 5.98 km) sit below both materiality thresholds. Were the profile consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, which establishes no pattern on the test POL-RD-06 actually states.
